https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/fia-stewa.text: Archie Griggs Updated Fri, 24 July 2026 at 12:05 pm UTC 0 Charles Leclerc escaped a penalty in Belgium after colliding with Oscar Piastri (Image: Getty) The FIA stewards have decided that Charles Leclerc should have been given a penalty at last weekend's Belgian Grand Prix . His clash with Oscar Piastri became a major talking point after the Ferrari driver escaped punishment, despite Lewis Hamilton being penalised for a similar incident earlier in the race . On the opening lap, Hamilton took out George Russell as the pair battled for position, resulting in the Mercedes driver being forced to retire. It looked nothing more than a racing incident, which Russell agreed with, but Hamilton was hit with a five-second penalty by the stewards. A handful of laps later, Leclerc tangled with Piastri by moving under braking, despite the Australian making no genuine attempt to overtake. However, on that occasion, the stewards decided not to hand down any penalties. That inconsistently was discussed at a meeting between drivers and the FIA ahead of this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix, according to The Race . It's claimed the stewards have now accepted that Leclerc should have been punished after a "lengthy debate" among those in attendance. The meeting was the first of two annual gatherings to discuss how incidents are dealt with and potential changes to F1's driving guidelines. The stewards have decided that Leclerc should have received a penalty (Image: Getty) The report adds that Leclerc argued the situation in Belgium was not entirely black-and-white, although he previously conceded that he may have overstepped the mark. Reflecting on his battle with Piastri, he said: "At the end of the day my view in the car is that I try to push the things to the limit. "I think with Oscar it was a bit on the other side, so that's probably not the way I want to race all the time. It's also risky for me at the end of the day. You're always trying to leave the smallest place available. That was maybe a bit too sketchy." Leclerc will be hoping to avoid any similar incidents in Hungary this weekend as Ferrari look to head into the summer break on a positive note. EXPRESS SPORT ON FB! https://hungarytoday.hu/viktor-orban-rea.text: Viktor Orbán Reacts to Ceuta Migration Crisis In their statements, Viktor Orbán and other politicians from the former governing parties pointed out that the European Union’s migration policy is responsible for the crisis in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. The FIDESZ chairman also expressed his support for Spain’s allies in the “Patriots for Europe” EU parliament group. The Spanish Ministry of the Interior says that 50,000 people have entered Ceuta illegally in recent days, whereas the Ceuta city government estimates the number at 60,000. Based on the latest figures, approximately 49,000 people have returned to Morocco. What is happening in Ceuta is yet another reminder of why Spain and Europe desperately need a VOX government,” Viktor Orbán stated on X . “Europe needs leaders who will defend its borders, restore order, and put the safety of their own citizens first,” he added. As a founder of the “Patriots for Europe” party family encouraged his Spanish ally with the words: “Santiago Abascal is ready to do exactly that. Vamos, Santiago!” 🇪🇸🇪🇺 What is happening in Ceuta is yet another reminder of why Spain, and Europe, desperately need a @vox_es government. Europe needs leaders who will defend its borders, restore order and put the safety of their own citizens first. @Santi_ABASCAL is ready to do exactly that.… pic.twitter.com/iCE9EKCGGk — Orbán Viktor (@PM_ViktorOrban) August 2, 2026 The current Irish EU Council Presidency has convened an extraordinary meeting of the EU Justice and Home Affairs Council for Tuesday, the Irish Times reported. The issue is expected to be raised not only in the Spanish Congress of Deputies but also at the European Parliament session in September, as several political groups are pushing for it. Allowing tens of thousands of illegals to break into Ceuta is anti-European. The pro-migration socialist government of Spain is undermining the security of European citizens and the entire Schengen area. All illegals must be removed from the territory of the EU! https://t.co/XuyhUpvmxL — András LÁSZLÓ MEP 🇭🇺 (@laszloan) July 31, 2026 MEP András László (FIDESZ) stated that the “Patriots for Europe” political group is also pushing to have the issue added to the agenda. On his social media page, the politician wrote: “Tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco and the sub-Saharan region have stormed Ceuta. They forced their way into the city by breaking through fences and tearing down walls. Just like in the Middle Ages. This is not merely illegal migration—it is an occupation.” The parliamentary group leader of the Christian Democratic People’s Party (KDNP) called on his Facebook page on Sunday for people to oppose the migration pact. Bence Rétvári—who described the images from Ceuta, Spain, as shocking—stated that the migration pact is an invitation to all illegal migrants to come to Europe. He pointed out that, under the pact, the European Union could declare a migration crisis and impose new obligations on member states if a country were suddenly exposed to very high migration pressure. In such a case, under EU regulations, the other member states must assume additional obligations, such as accepting illegal migrants or conducting the entire immigration and asylum process in another member state. This is no trivial matter. It now poses a risk to every EU member state when tens of thousands of illegal migrants turn up in one EU country,” said the Christian Democrat. Bence Rétvári emphasized that there were no such scenes in Hungary and that tens of thousands of illegal migrants were not appearing there because the Orbán government had erected a fence and was protecting the southern border with legal and physical border barriers. He made it clear that the Migration Pact would exploit this situation and that, due to the irresponsible migration policies of other countries, the remaining countries would have to assume responsibility. The parliamentary group leader recalled that Hungary was the country that had never supported the adoption of the Migration Pact, yet it had been pushed through nonetheless. Now, he said, the first crisis situation had arisen. Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced on Saturday that Prime Minister Péter Magyar, along with 21 heads of state and government of the European Union, had also signed a letter criticizing the migration policy of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The signatories believe that the Spanish government’s measures weaken the protection of the EU’s external borders and are calling for a coordinated approach at the EU level to strengthen those borders. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cn0n.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, The counting of votes from Thursday's poll is still going on By Dingindaba Buyoya Reporting from Lusaka Published 17 August 2026, 08:31 BST Updated 23 minutes ago Security forces in Zambia have seized weapons and arrested 11 people, including senior opposition figures, allegedly involved in an insurrection plot, the government has said. The leading opposition candidate in last Thursday's presidential election, Brian Mundubile, was also found at the scene of the raid in the capital, Lusaka, according to the country's top civil servant Patrick Kangwa. In an interview with the BBC, Mundubile dismissed the accusations as "total fabrications", saying security forces staged an assassination attempt on his life during a raid at his home on Friday. With results from more than half of the constituencies announced, he is trailing incumbent Hakainde Hichilema. Mundubile had earlier claimed victory and alleged there were voting irregularities. Giving details about the raid, Kangwa said the individuals arrested were connected to "military plans involving foreign nationals and illegal military training camps". He added that they posed "a serious threat to state security" and held "high-grade military weapons", ammunition and other materials intended for use in an armed insurrection. He alleged that shots were fired at law enforcement officers leading to an exchange of fire. Mundubile however told the BBC that there was no militia at his home. "It's unfortunate that senior government officials would present themselves before the entire nation to make such falsehoods," he told BBC Focus on Africa. According to Kangwa, among those arrested were Patrick Mwansa, the husband of Tasila Lungu, the daughter of former Zambian President Edgar Lungu, and other politicians. The suspects are being held in custody at various police stations in Lusaka. Mundubile described the raid to the BBC in detail, saying armed personnel knocked down the gate with an armoured vehicle, broke doors and windows and opened fire. "They were basically shooting indiscriminately. They directed two shots towards me. Like I've always said, it was just by God's grace that I survived. "So they came in to kill us," he said. Mundubile said former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was shot while he and his wife were present. He said Kafwaya, whose whereabouts remain unknown, was bleeding and he urged the officers to take him to hospital. Mundubile said his family remains traumatised. "My children saw their uncleâ¦ bleeding profusely and being dragged like an animalâ¦ 80 soldiers coming into the house, shooting indiscriminately and breaking doors and windows down is not an experience anybody would want to go through." He said he and his family had not returned home since Friday and felt unsafe. On the day following the election, he maintained that his campaign's parallel vote tabulation showed him in the lead and repeated allegations of irregularities, without providing detailed evidence The authorities denied the claims of vote rigging and in preliminary statements observers described election day as largely peaceful and orderly. They did however raise concerns about late electoral reforms, media freedom and access to the media in the run-up to the poll. The mood remains stable as Zambians await the full results of the election, although some uncertainty has emerged following the government's announcement of the raid. However, there is a heightened security police presence in some parts of the capital. Mundubile had made a series of allegations about the electoral process, including reports of military involvement at tallying centres and irregularities involving ballot boxes. He later said he was being interrogated by Zambian army officers over two videos he released and alleged he had been assaulted while in custody, which authorities denied. He also accused Tanzania of sending individuals to interfere in the election, an allegation the Tanzanian government firmly rejected as false and unfounded. Zambia's electoral commission briefly suspended the counting and announcement of results on Friday, citing violence against polling staff and theft of marked ballot papers. It lifted the suspension the same day, saying the security threat had been contained. Both the European Union (EU) and the southern African (Sadc) observer missions have since expressed concern over the suspension of the vote counting. On Saturday, Sadc said it had created "uncertainty and anxiety" while the EU mission said any such interruption should be clearly explained, legally grounded and proportionate. The EU mission's chief observer Michael McNamara said the elections took place "against a backdrop of constrained democratic space". He said even though the elections were "genuinely competitive" the conditions in which the candidates competed were "uneven". He cited the blurring of lines between state and the party, including state media coverage being "heavily biased" to favour the ruling party. "It is important that the remaining stages of the process are conducted calmly, transparently, and in full accordance with Zambian law and the procedures in place." https://artsound.fm/news/an-evening-for-.text: Search in the website: Home / News / Events / An Evening for Nepal Live Music, Good Company, and a Cause Worth Showing Up For There’s something special about turning out for a good cause in person. Not just donating from behind a screen, but actually being there: sharing a room, a drink, and a few songs with fellow Canberrans who care about the same thing you do. That’s exactly what’s on offer on Sunday 20 September , when ArtSound FM joins forces with NKSSP Canberra (the Nepali Art, Culture and Literature Academy) for a warm, welcoming evening at the Polish White Eagle Club in Turner, all in support of families in Nepal whose lives have been upended by catastrophic flooding. You may have already heard the news: in late August, flash flooding and landslides tore through communities along the Nepal-China border, destroying homes, roads and livelihoods in a matter of hours. It’s the kind of disaster that’s easy to read about and hard to picture; until you think about it as neighbours losing everything overnight, with children and elderly residents among the most vulnerable. This is where a bit of Canberra community spirit can genuinely help. The Emergency Action Alliance brings together some of Australia’s most trusted aid organisations to get help where it’s needed most, quickly and efficiently. And every single dollar raised on the night — 100% of event profits — goes straight to their Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal. A relaxed Sunday evening, done properly This isn’t a solemn affair. Quite the opposite. Think of it as a proper community get-together: good music, a well-stocked bar, and the chance to catch up with familiar faces while doing something worthwhile. Two excellent local acts will be keeping the night lively: The Devil and The Bunny and The Daisy Coolective , both known for bringing warmth and energy to a room. The bar will be open all evening, with bar snacks on hand to keep you going. Whether you come for the music, the cause, or simply a pleasant Sunday evening out, you’ll leave knowing your ticket made a genuine difference to families who need it. The details When: Sunday 20 September 2026, 6:00pm–8:00pm (doors open 5:30pm) Where: Polish White Eagle Club (The Polo), 38 David Street, Turner ACT 2612 Tickets: $25 per adult, children under 12 free Music: The Devil and The Bunny + The Daisy Coolective Refreshments: Full bar service, with snacks available Where the money goes: 100% of profits donated directly to the Emergency Action Alliance Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal Make a Difference – Buy a Ticket Can’t make it on the night? You can still be part of this effort. Donations can be made directly to the appeal at any time: Online: emergencyaction.org.au/nepal-flood-appeal By phone: 1300 939 000 Every contribution, large or small, helps provide emergency shelter, clean water and medical care to families rebuilding their lives. We hope to see you there on the 20th — bring a friend, bring your appetite for good music, and let’s show Nepal that Canberra is standing with them.
